label: Lined up on runway 30R, Dubai
Gear down
flydubai 1073, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 (A6-FKF), lines up on runway 30R at Dubai International for Tel Aviv, a flight of about three hours.
Take-off roll
Lift-off
Climb
Gear up (not recorded; estimated)

On the flight deck the captain, an Indian national, is flying; the first officer, an Omani who joined flydubai about a year earlier, is monitoring. Two more flydubai pilots ride in the cabin, rostered to fly the aircraft back to Dubai.
Level at 32,000 ft
Cruise
From 03:54 to 05:16 the open networks hear nothing over Saudi Arabia; this stretch follows other receivers. The aircraft climbs to 34,000 ft at 04:09 and flies on west past Rafha and Sakaka.
Cruise at 34,000 ft over northern Saudi Arabia
Two hours and eleven minutes after take-off, flydubai 1073 cruises west over Saudi Arabia's Al Jawf region at 34,000 ft.
Descent begins; the selected altitude still reads 34,000 ft
At 05:21:09 the aircraft starts down, reaching 2,900 ft/min. The altitude set on the autopilot panel, which the aircraft keeps broadcasting, still reads 34,000 ft: no descent had been selected.
Abrupt pitch changes; the dive steepens
Dive

From 05:21:44 the broadcast pressure altitude jumps by up to 1,000 ft within a second while the GPS positions stay smooth, and the ground speed falls from 441 to 377 kt in five seconds: violent pitch changes. Then the aircraft dives, turning right.
Saudi Arabia's preliminary inquiry: the first officer attacked the captain. By Israeli accounts he stabbed him with a knife and the cockpit's emergency axe, and tried to crash the aircraft.

At 05:22:13, at 27,950 ft and diving at over 20,000 ft per minute, the aircraft drops out of the open networks' reach for nine minutes. Other receivers keep hearing it: over 14,000 ft lost in under 30 seconds.
It pulls out at about 16,600 ft at 05:22:40, turning hard right through north-east at 598 kt over the ground: far beyond the 737 MAX's maximum operating speed.
Most of the rudder torn away (when, exactly, is not known)
Bottom of the dive: 16,600 ft, 598 kt

The wounded captain fights him off long enough to release the cockpit door. Cabin crew and passengers, Israelis among them, break in and overpower the first officer; one passenger pulls back on the controls as he had seen on television. The two off-duty flydubai pilots take over.

Photos at Tabuk show most of the rudder torn from the fin, from its lower third almost to the tip, most likely by the speed of the dive. It is drawn gone from the dive's fastest moment; when it went is not known.
Zoom climb to 21,725 ft
Down again, turning north-west
A zoom climb to 21,725 ft at 05:23:23, then down again to 14,950 ft by 05:24:18, turning north-west.
Low point 13,675 ft
Open networks hear it again: 15,000 ft, squawk 7700
15,000 ft, emergency
The open networks hear it again at 05:31:26: level at 15,000 ft, heading north-west toward Jordan. The selected altitude now reads 15,000 ft. The transponder code is 7700, a general emergency.
Emergency status: unlawful interference (7500)
At 05:35:17 the transponder's emergency status changes to unlawful interference, the meaning of code 7500, used for a hijacking. Israel scrambles fighter jets.
Enters Jordanian airspace
Turns back, 200° to the left
Turn back
Over Jordan, south of Al-Jafr, the aircraft turns left through 200° at up to 24° of bank. The heading selected on the autopilot panel changes to 100°: back toward Saudi Arabia.

Israel's assessment: an attempted suicide terror attack. Israeli intelligence says the first officer was radicalized over the past year and acted alone, meaning to bring down the aircraft with its 174 passengers, most of them Israelis. Netanyahu: "clear he was suicidal"; Defence Minister Katz: "an attempted jihadist terror attack".
Back in Saudi airspace
Selected heading 130°
The selected heading turns to 130°, south-east, at 15,000 ft with code 7500 still set.
The UAE, which takes the first officer over from Saudi Arabia two days later, is investigating a link to terrorism and any prior planning. There is no official finding on the motive yet.
At 05:53:32 the open networks lose the aircraft for good. Other receivers follow it south-east, then south and south-west toward Tabuk, still at 15,000 ft.
Heads south-west for Tabuk
Out of ground receivers' coverage
Descent to Tabuk (reconstructed)
At 06:13 the aircraft leaves the ground receivers' coverage. After that only satellites heard it, twice in the air: the descent to Tabuk is reconstructed between those fixes.
Satellite fix: 5,475 ft, squawk 7700
06:28:37: a satellite hears it 15 nm north-east of Tabuk at 5,475 ft, heading south-south-west at 205 kt, squawking 7700.
The next fix, 15 minutes later, is only 14 nm away: the aircraft flew about three times that distance, and how is not known. It is drawn here as a long right-hand circuit onto runway 31.
Gear down (not recorded; estimated)
Final approach, runway 31
Satellite fix: 3.2 nm out on runway 31
06:43:39, the last airborne fix: 3.2 nm out on runway 31's centreline at 3,375 ft, descending 960 ft/min at 185 kt, on a normal 3° glidepath.
Touchdown, runway 31 (~06:45)
Landing

It lands on runway 31 at Tabuk at about 06:45, flown by the two off-duty flydubai pilots. Saudi authorities detain the first officer; the captain, badly wounded, goes to hospital. All 174 passengers are safe.
